name: France
tagline: Paris boulevards to Riviera blue — the classic Europe trip, done properly
hero_description: France pairs the world's most-visited museum city with its most glamorous coastline. Start with Paris — the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre's glass pyramid, Versailles' Hall of Mirrors — then take the fast train south to where the Alps meet the Mediterranean: Nice's seven-kilometre promenade, the perched village of Èze, and tiny Monaco next door.
best_time_to_visit: April–May and September–October — mild weather, shorter museum queues and shoulder-season pricing; the Riviera stays pleasant nearly year-round, and March means the shortest lines at the Eiffel Tower and Louvre.

top_attractions.name: Eiffel Tower
top_attractions.description: Built in 1889 for the Exposition Universelle and now around 330 m tall with its antennas — take the lifts to the summit at sunset for the city turning gold.

top_attractions.name: The Louvre
top_attractions.description: The world's most-visited museum, entered through I. M. Pei's 1989 glass pyramid — the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo top most lists, but the medieval fortress foundations below surprise everyone.

top_attractions.name: Palace of Versailles
top_attractions.description: Louis XIV's UNESCO-listed palace 20 km from Paris — its Hall of Mirrors runs 73 m with 357 mirrors, and the gardens' musical fountain shows run in season.

top_attractions.name: Seine river cruise
top_attractions.description: The riverbanks themselves are UNESCO-listed — glide past Notre-Dame, restored and reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire.

top_attractions.name: Nice & the Promenade des Anglais
top_attractions.description: Seven kilometres of Mediterranean seafront backed by an old town whose flower market fills Cours Saleya — Nice's Riviera townscape earned its own UNESCO listing in 2021.

top_attractions.name: Monaco & Èze
top_attractions.description: The world's second-smallest country — the 1863 Casino de Monte-Carlo and walkable F1 corners — reached along a corniche that passes Èze, a medieval village perched 430 m above the sea.

activities: Sunset ride to the Eiffel Tower summit
Versailles day trip with the Hall of Mirrors and gardens
Montmartre walk up to Sacré-Cœur and the artists' square
TGV journey from Paris to the Riviera
Cycle the Promenade des Anglais and browse the Cours Saleya market
Corniche day trip to Èze village and Monte-Carlo
